A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PREDFT research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved into the expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Narratives decoding experiments, predictive-coding verification, ROI and prediction-distance analyses, ablations, and decoding-error analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original Narratives results and adds LeBel dataset experiments, additional baseline comparisons, prediction-length analyses, and shuffled-input controls.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a linear-layer encoder for 2D brain-surface inputs alongside the existing volumetric 3D-CNN encoder. The main and side Transformers, predictive cross-attention, and joint losses remain. The newly explicit description of discarding the side decoder during inference does not establish a change to the earlier procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only Narratives, using 230 selected subjects. v2 retains this coverage and adds three subjects from LeBel's dataset for predictive-coding verification and language decoding, substantially extending the evaluated data and population.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates UniCoRN as its external decoding comparator. v2 additionally evaluates Tang's method, BrainLLM, and MapGuide on LeBel's dataset in Table 1, while retaining UniCoRN for Narratives in Table 2. Tang's method and BrainLLM were discussed but explicitly excluded from v1's experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds within-subject evaluation using ten LeBel fMRI frames spanning 20 seconds, introduces BERTScore-F1, and evaluates prediction-length/distance grids. Appendix A.4 also changes the reported training budget from v1's 20 epochs to 40. This is a reported setting revision; unchanged Narratives scores do not establish whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds shuffled-fMRI controls testing reliance on ordered brain input (Tables 6–7) and extensive joint prediction-length/distance analyses (Figure 7 and Appendix C). ROI, side-network, and loss-weight analyses also extend to LeBel's subjects. The original Narratives positional-error analysis and decoding examples remain, rather than constituting new analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies ten-fold held-out cross-validation for estimating each subject's brain score. The 95% confidence intervals across subjects were already reported in v1 Figure 1 and remain in v2 Figure 12. No increase in repeated training runs or new decoding-table uncertainty reporting is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including LeBel PREDFT BLEU-1 scores of 34.95, 32.46, and 33.22 in Table 1, BERTScores, and shuffled-input results. Original Narratives BLEU/ROUGE results are retained, so these additions are not same-setting performance gains. One added value is inconsistent: subject-2 PREDFT BERTScore is 83.52 in Table 1 but 82.52 in Table 6.

T1.justification: Section 2 changes the definition of prediction distance from the distance to the last future word in v1 to the first future word in v2. For fixed distance and length, these definitions specify different word windows, without an explicit reconciliation. The principal attention, loss, and information-loss-slope equations remain.

C1.justification: The central novelty and contribution—using a predictive side network to improve fMRI-to-text decoding—remain. The abstract replaces the Narratives-specific state-of-the-art statement and 27.8% BLEU-1 figure with a claim of outperforming decoding models on several metrics across two datasets, expanding the stated empirical scope.

C2.justification: v2 revises limitations after addressing the single-dataset, cross-subject-only, and fixed-prediction-length restrictions, and identifies visual stimuli and other signal modalities as remaining boundaries. Appendices F–G add distinctions between fluency and semantic fidelity across decoder families and recommend semantic-level evaluation. The predictive-coding debate and information-loss explanation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: explicit subject/stimulus separation rules, dataset-specific parcellation and tokenizers, PCA reduction from 768 to 20 dimensions, ridge penalization settings, 18 CNN layers, approximately 200 million parameters, and training from scratch. It also explains inference explicitly. Most are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds MapGuide to the decoding literature, recent works by Xia et al. and Yin et al., and references supporting BERTScore, PCA, and scikit-learn. The central research positioning remains, including Antonello and Huth's alternative explanation, which moves into Appendix G.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites explanatory passages and reorganizes the narrative. The main Discussion becomes a shorter Conclusion, while discussion and case studies move to dedicated appendices. Experimental documentation is divided into multiple subsections and appendices, and separate Limitations and Ethics sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout and substantially redesigns its displays. v2 adds simplified training/inference and encoder diagrams, a notation table, heatmaps, and additional comparison tables. The original detailed architecture moves to Figure 8, and retained ROI results appear both graphically and in appendix tables.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important limitations explicitly acknowledged in v1 through a second dataset, within-subject evaluation, and variable prediction lengths. Additional external baselines, shuffled-input controls, and substantially fuller implementation documentation strengthen the evidence and reproducibility. The unexplained training-budget revision and conflicting subject-2 BERTScore limit precision, but do not outweigh these substantial gains. The improvement comes from stronger evaluation and documentation, not an established increase in same-setting performance.
